ui.tip_drop_any_downloaded_file_anywhere: Tip: drop any downloaded file anywhere on the dock — a Bible (.zip, .json, USFM), hymns, a service schedule or a backup. HymnFlow works out what it is, unzips and converts it for you.
ui.hymnflow_never_downloads_anything_itself: HymnFlow never downloads anything itself. Pick a language, open the link, save the file, then drop it onto the Bible card above — no unzipping or converting needed. Check each translation’s license.
ui.hymns_services_and_settings_are_stored: Hymns, services and settings are stored in this browser. A snapshot is taken automatically each time the dock opens, and deleted hymns or services can be undone for a few seconds.
ui.usage_report_each_hymn_put_on: Usage report: each hymn put on screen is logged on this device (date, title, CCLI number) so you can report to CCLI. Nothing is sent anywhere.
ui.bibles_are_stored_separately_and_are: Bibles are stored separately and are not touched by backup or restore. OBS connection details and password are never written to a backup file.
ui.showing_copyrighted_lyrics_on_a_livestre: showing copyrighted lyrics on a livestream usually needs a streaming license in addition to a standard church copyright license (for example CCLI or OneLicense). Requirements differ by country and platform — check with your licensing provider. Public-domain hymns need none. Record each hymn’s copyright and CCLI number in its edit form.
ui.you_are_responsible_for_having_the: you are responsible for having the right to use the translations you import. Public-domain and openly licensed texts are fine; others need permission from the publisher.

ui.take_the_screen_down_without_losing: Take the screen down without losing your place (B)
ui.bring_back_what_was_on_screen: Bring back what was on screen before Blank / Clear (Z)
ui.import_a_service_schedule_from_a: Import a service schedule from a text file
ui.skip_the_confidence_preview_planned_scri: Skip the confidence preview: planned scripture items go straight to the overlay when activated
ui.on_the_last_verse_the_first: On the last verse, the first Next only arms the advance; a second press within a few seconds moves to the next service item
